text: Two similar triangles have perimeters $15\text{ cm}$ and $25\text{ cm}$. If the area of the smaller triangle is $54\text{ cm}^{2}$, the area of the larger triangle is
answer: Correct option: B) $150\text{ cm}^{2}$. The ratio of corresponding sides is $15 : 25 = 3 : 5$, so the ratio of areas is $9 : 25$. Area of larger triangle $= 54 \times \frac{25}{9} = 150\text{ cm}^{2}$.

text: The diagonals of a rhombus are $16\text{ cm}$ and $30\text{ cm}$. The perimeter of the rhombus is
answer: Correct option: B) $68\text{ cm}$. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so each side is $\sqrt{8^{2} + 15^{2}} = 17\text{ cm}$. Perimeter $= 4 \times 17 = 68\text{ cm}$.

text:
Assertion (A): Triangles with sides $3\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$, $15\text{ cm}$, $20\text{ cm}$ are similar.
Reason (R): Two triangles are similar if their corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: D) A is false but R is true. Pairing sides in order, $\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}$ but $\frac{7}{20} \ne \frac{1}{3}$, so the sides are not proportional and A is false. R is the SSS similarity criterion and is true.

text: $ABCD$ is a trapezium with $AB \parallel DC$, $AB = 12\text{ cm}$ and $DC = 20\text{ cm}$. A line through the point of intersection $O$ of the diagonals, parallel to $AB$, meets $AD$ at $P$ and $BC$ at $Q$. Then $PQ =$
answer: Correct option: B) $15\text{ cm}$. In $\triangle ADC$, $PO \parallel DC$ gives $\frac{PO}{DC} = \frac{AO}{AC}$. Since $\triangle AOB \sim \triangle COD$, $\frac{AO}{OC} = \frac{12}{20}$, so $\frac{AO}{AC} = \frac{12}{32}$ and $PO = 20 \times \frac{12}{32} = 7.5\text{ cm}$. Similarly $OQ = 7.5\text{ cm}$, so $PQ = 15\text{ cm}$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B = 90^\circ$, $AB = 15\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 20\text{ cm}$. $BD \perp AC$ with $D$ on $AC$. Then $DC =$
answer: Correct option: C) $16\text{ cm}$. $AC = \sqrt{15^{2} + 20^{2}} = 25\text{ cm}$. Since $\triangle BDC \sim \triangle ABC$, $BC^{2} = DC \times AC$, so $DC = \frac{400}{25} = 16\text{ cm}$.

text: The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio $16 : 49$. If the perimeter of the smaller triangle is $36\text{ cm}$, find the perimeter of the larger triangle.
answer: Ratio of corresponding sides $= \sqrt{\frac{16}{49}} = \frac{4}{7}$. Perimeters of similar triangles are in the same ratio, so $\frac{36}{P} = \frac{4}{7}$ and $P = \frac{36 \times 7}{4} = 63$. The perimeter of the larger triangle is $63\text{ cm}$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is a point on $BC$ such that $AD \perp BC$ and $AD^{2} = BD \times CD$. Prove that $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$.
answer: From $AD^{2} = BD \times CD$, $\frac{BD}{AD} = \frac{AD}{CD}$. Also $\angle ADB = \angle CDA = 90^\circ$. By SAS similarity, $\triangle DBA \sim \triangle DAC$, so $\angle BAD = \angle ACD$. Then $\angle BAC = \angle BAD + \angle DAC = \angle ACD + \angle DAC = 90^\circ$, because $\angle ADC = 90^\circ$ makes the other two angles of $\triangle ADC$ sum to $90^\circ$. Hence $\angle BAC = 90^\circ$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ lies on $AB$ and $E$ lies on $AC$ with $AD = 3.5\text{ cm}$, $DB = 5.25\text{ cm}$, $AE = 4\text{ cm}$ and $EC = 6\text{ cm}$. (a) Show that $DE \parallel BC$. (b) If $BC = 12.5\text{ cm}$, find $DE$.
answer: (a) $\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{3.5}{5.25} = \frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{AE}{EC} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$. The line $DE$ divides $AB$ and $AC$ in the same ratio, so by the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem, $DE \parallel BC$. (b) $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$ (AA), so $\frac{DE}{BC} = \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{3.5}{8.75} = \frac{2}{5}$. Hence $DE = \frac{2}{5} \times 12.5 = 5\text{ cm}$.

text: $ABCD$ is a trapezium with $AB \parallel DC$, $AB = 28\text{ cm}$ and $DC = 14\text{ cm}$. $E$ lies on $AD$ and $F$ lies on $BC$ such that $EF \parallel AB$ and $AE : ED = 3 : 4$. Find $EF$.
answer: Join $AC$ and let it meet $EF$ at $G$. In $\triangle ADC$, $EG \parallel DC$, so $\frac{EG}{DC} = \frac{AE}{AD} = \frac{3}{7}$ and $EG = 6\text{ cm}$. Since $EF \parallel AB \parallel DC$, $\frac{CF}{CB} = \frac{DE}{DA} = \frac{4}{7}$. In $\triangle CAB$, $GF \parallel AB$, so $\frac{GF}{AB} = \frac{CF}{CB} = \frac{4}{7}$ and $GF = 16\text{ cm}$. Therefore $EF = 6 + 16 = 22\text{ cm}$.

text: In an acute-angled $\triangle ABC$, $BE \perp AC$ with $E$ on $AC$, and $CF \perp AB$ with $F$ on $AB$. (a) Prove that $\triangle AEB \sim \triangle AFC$. (b) If $AB = 12\text{ cm}$, $AC = 15\text{ cm}$ and $AF = 4.5\text{ cm}$, find $AE$.
answer: (a) In $\triangle AEB$ and $\triangle AFC$: $\angle AEB = \angle AFC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle A$ is common. By AA, $\triangle AEB \sim \triangle AFC$. (b) Corresponding sides are proportional: $\frac{AE}{AF} = \frac{AB}{AC}$, so $AE = 4.5 \times \frac{12}{15} = 3.6\text{ cm}$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. The line $BE$ meets $AC$ at $F$. Prove that $AF = \frac{1}{3} AC$.
answer: Draw $DG \parallel BF$ meeting $AC$ at $G$. In $\triangle CBF$, $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $DG \parallel BF$, so by the Basic Proportionality Theorem $G$ is the midpoint of $CF$, i.e. $CG = GF$. In $\triangle ADG$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$ and $EF \parallel DG$, so $F$ is the midpoint of $AG$, i.e. $AF = FG$. Hence $AF = FG = GC$, and $AF = \frac{1}{3} AC$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 12\text{ cm}$, $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 10\text{ cm}$. $D$ lies on $AB$ with $AD = 3\text{ cm}$ and $E$ lies on $AC$ with $AE = 4.5\text{ cm}$. Show that $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB$ and find $DE$.
answer: In $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ACB$: $\frac{AD}{AC} = \frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{AE}{AB} = \frac{4.5}{12} = \frac{3}{8}$, and $\angle DAE = \angle CAB$ (common). By SAS similarity, $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ACB$. Then $\frac{DE}{CB} = \frac{3}{8}$, so $DE = \frac{3}{8} \times 10 = 3.75\text{ cm}$.

text: A lamp is fixed at the top of a vertical post standing on level ground. A girl $1.6\text{ m}$ tall stands $3\text{ m}$ from the foot of the post, and her shadow is $2\text{ m}$ long. (a) Find the height of the lamp above the ground. (b) She walks away until she is $6\text{ m}$ from the foot of the post. Find the new length of her shadow.
answer: The lamp, the top of her head and the tip of the shadow are in a line. Triangles formed by the post and by the girl are similar (AA, both right-angled with a common angle at the tip of the shadow). (a) $\frac{h}{1.6} = \frac{3 + 2}{2}$, so $h = 1.6 \times 2.5 = 4\text{ m}$. (b) With shadow $s$: $\frac{4}{1.6} = \frac{6 + s}{s}$, so $2.5s = 6 + s$, $1.5s = 6$ and $s = 4\text{ m}$. The lamp is $4\text{ m}$ high and the new shadow is $4\text{ m}$ long.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ lies on $AB$ and $E$ lies on $AC$ with $DE \parallel BC$. The area of quadrilateral $DBCE$ is $8$ times the area of $\triangle ADE$. (a) Find $AD : DB$. (b) If $BC = 18\text{ cm}$, find $DE$.
answer: Let area of $\triangle ADE = k$. Then area of $\triangle ABC = k + 8k = 9k$. $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$, so $\frac{\text{ar}(ADE)}{\text{ar}(ABC)} = \left(\frac{AD}{AB}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{9}$, giving $\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{1}{3}$. (a) $AD : DB = 1 : 2$. (b) $\frac{DE}{BC} = \frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{1}{3}$, so $DE = 6\text{ cm}$.

text: The sides of a right-angled triangle are $9\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$ and $15\text{ cm}$. Similar triangles are drawn on all three sides, each side being the corresponding side of its triangle. The area of the triangle on the $9\text{ cm}$ side is $27\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find the areas of the triangles on the other two sides and verify that the area on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the other two.
answer: Areas of similar triangles are proportional to the squares of corresponding sides. Area on $12\text{ cm}$ side $= 27 \times \frac{12^{2}}{9^{2}} = 27 \times \frac{144}{81} = 48\text{ cm}^{2}$. Area on $15\text{ cm}$ side $= 27 \times \frac{225}{81} = 75\text{ cm}^{2}$. Check: $27 + 48 = 75$, so the area on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas on the other two sides, as $9^{2} + 12^{2} = 15^{2}$.

text: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 17\text{ cm}$, $AC = 10\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 21\text{ cm}$. $AD \perp BC$ with $D$ on $BC$. Find $AD$, the area of the triangle, and the length of the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$.
answer: Let $BD = x$, so $DC = 21 - x$. From $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$: $AD^{2} = 17^{2} - x^{2} = 10^{2} - (21 - x)^{2}$. So $289 - x^{2} = 100 - 441 + 42x - x^{2}$, giving $630 = 42x$ and $x = 15$. Then $AD = \sqrt{289 - 225} = 8\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 21 \times 8 = 84\text{ cm}^{2}$. If $h$ is the perpendicular from $B$ to $AC$, $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times h = 84$, so $h = 16.8\text{ cm}$.

text:
Case study: A surveyor wants the width of a canal without crossing it. A tree $T$ stands on the far bank. She marks the point $P$ on the near bank directly opposite the tree, so $PT$ is perpendicular to the bank. She walks along the bank to $Q$ with $PQ = 36\text{ m}$, and fixes a peg $R$ on $PQ$ with $PR = 24\text{ m}$. At $Q$ she turns at a right angle, away from the canal, and walks to a point $U$ from which the peg $R$ and the tree $T$ are in one line. She measures $QU = 9\text{ m}$.
(i) Name the criterion by which $\triangle PRT \sim \triangle QRU$. [1]
(ii) Find the ratio $PR : RQ$ and hence the ratio $TR : RU$. [1]
(iii) Find the width of the canal and the distance $TU$. [2]
answer: (i) $\angle P = \angle Q = 90^\circ$ and $\angle PRT = \angle QRU$ (vertically opposite), so the triangles are similar by the AA criterion. (ii) $RQ = 36 - 24 = 12\text{ m}$, so $PR : RQ = 24 : 12 = 2 : 1$. By similarity $TR : RU = PR : RQ = 2 : 1$. (iii) $\frac{PT}{QU} = \frac{PR}{RQ} = 2$, so $PT = 18\text{ m}$, the width of the canal. In right $\triangle QRU$, $RU = \sqrt{12^{2} + 9^{2}} = 15\text{ m}$, so $TR = 30\text{ m}$ and $TU = 30 + 15 = 45\text{ m}$.

text:
Case study: A farmer owns two triangular fields, $ABC$ and $PQR$, with $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$. The sides of field $ABC$ are $AB = 9\text{ m}$, $BC = 12\text{ m}$ and $CA = 15\text{ m}$. The longest side $PR$ of field $PQR$ is $25\text{ m}$.
(i) Find the ratio of the sides of the two fields. [1]
(ii) Show that field $ABC$ is right-angled and name the vertex of the right angle. [1]
(iii) Find the area of field $PQR$ and the cost of fencing it at ₹50 per metre. [2]
answer: (i) $CA$ and $PR$ are corresponding longest sides, so $\frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{15}{25} = \frac{3}{5}$ and the sides are in the ratio $3 : 5$. (ii) $AB^{2} + BC^{2} = 81 + 144 = 225 = CA^{2}$, so by the converse of Pythagoras theorem the angle opposite $CA$ is a right angle, i.e. at $B$. (iii) $PQ = 15\text{ m}$, $QR = 20\text{ m}$, $PR = 25\text{ m}$. Area of $ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12 = 54\text{ m}^{2}$, so area of $PQR = 54 \times \frac{25}{9} = 150\text{ m}^{2}$. Perimeter of $PQR = 15 + 20 + 25 = 60\text{ m}$, so fencing costs $60 \times 50 = $ ₹3000.
